proof.text: The coefficient construction supplies the finite rings $A_n=\mathcal O_E/(t^n)$, their quotient maps, and the completed sheaves $R_W=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_W$ on the chosen small pro-etale sites. The site and module-category definitions give ordinary unbounded derived categories. The map $\underline A_W\to R_W$ and each projection $R_W\to(A_n)_W$ define restriction-of-scalars functors; restriction leaves the underlying sheaf and maps unchanged. The completed-pullback datum gives the structural map $f^{-1}R_Y\to R_X$ and identifies inverse images of the constant and finite quotient sheaves, so the symbols $U_W$, $V_{W,n}$ and the reduction maps in the statement have the asserted types.

proof.text: Regard the maps $\underline A_Y\to R_Y$ and $R_Y\to(A_n)_Y$ as coefficient changes on the identity underlying topos. The two factorizations of the same morphism of ringed topoi (first change coefficients and then apply $f$, or first apply $f$ and then change coefficients) are covered by the canonical K-injective composition comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. Its naturality gives the displayed isomorphisms $U_YF_R\cong F_AU_X$ and $F_RV_{X,n}\cong V_{Y,n}F_n$. The comparison is normalized by the resolution map in that node, so it is the canonical one rather than an arbitrary isomorphism. Exactness of each restriction-of-scalars functor follows directly from its unchanged underlying abelian sheaf, hence the termwise restrictions used here define functors on the unbounded derived categories.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition, applied to the two coefficient factorizations

proof.text: For $m\ge n$, the finite-ring comparison of [lem-weil-proetale-direct-image-restriction-of-scalars] is the comparison from Step 2 for $A_m\to A_n$: both have the stated value on a K-injective complex and its restricted resolution. Coherence follows from the universal property in [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived], not from objectwise naturality alone. For three coefficient restrictions, the two composites of derived comparisons, precomposed with the common underived-to-derived transformation, are both the transformation induced by the same termwise composite of ring maps. Injectivity of the universal-property bijection makes those composites equal. The same argument with an identity restriction gives the unit law. Thus every finite quotient square, and every successive-restriction triangle, commutes.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition; coherence by the universal property of total derived functors

proof.text: Check the coefficient hypotheses once. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], $A$ is a principal ideal domain, hence Noetherian, and $t$ is a nonzero nonunit. The residue field is finite; [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients] gives finiteness of every $A_n$ and surjectivity of its quotient maps. In particular $A/(t)$ is additive torsion. The exact sequence $0\to A\xrightarrow{t^n}A\to A_n\to0$ is a finite free resolution, verifying perfection. Also $A\cong\varprojlim A_n$: lifts $a_n\in A$ of a compatible family satisfy $a_{n+1}-a_n\in t^nA$, so are Cauchy and converge by [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-complete]. Their limit is in the closed valuation ball $A$ and gives every prescribed residue; uniqueness follows since $\bigcap_n t^nA=0$ by the valuation. These verify the coefficient hypotheses of both the adic-datum proposition and the coefficient-system lemma used below.

source.place: Tag 099N, lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case: verification of the Noetherian coefficient specialization

proof.text: Let $J=\mathbf N_{\ge1}^{\mathrm{op}}$. The small diagram site of [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization] realizes sheaves on the tower topos as $J$-diagrams. A module over its ring object $B_W=((A_n)_W)_n$ is precisely a family of modules with quotient-linear transitions: the action and module axioms are componentwise. Restriction along the ring map from the constant diagram $R_W$ to $B_W$ is exact and sends $M_\bullet$ to the strict $R_W$-tower $(V_{W,n}M_n)_n$. Apply the ringed-topos composition comparison of Step 2 on these diagram topoi, to the two factorizations of this restriction and levelwise $f_*$. This yields an isomorphism of derived strict-tower functors. The evaluation identifications in [lem-pur-coefficient-system-derived-comparison] and [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison] identify its evaluations with $F_RV_{X,n}\cong V_{Y,n}F_n$. Their normalization is the K-injective comparison already fixed. Step 3 gives the restriction coherence. This constructs the comparison before evaluation, so it includes the strict diagram assertion of the item.

proof.text: Choose the reduction tower on a single flat-term K-flat representative as in [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower]. It is the strict quotient tower of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. There is a small distinction between completeness conventions to resolve. The condition of [def-weil-derived-complete] supplies a Roos triangle, hence an isomorphism of $K$ with the derived inverse limit of its quotient tower, using the Roos triangle of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. It does not itself choose the canonical completion morphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence], that quotient-limit object is the Koszul completion of $K$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-completion-reflector], it is locally derived complete. Thus $K$, being isomorphic to it, is locally derived complete as well. The same reflector lemma now makes its canonical Koszul unit invertible; the unit-compatible comparison in [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] makes the canonical quotient-tower unit invertible. Thus $K$ is locally derived $t$-complete and its functorial Koszul unit $\kappa_K$ is invertible, without selecting an arbitrary cone isomorphism; Step 7 compares this with the explicit model of the next proposition.

source.place: Tags 099L and 099M, section-derived-completion-noetherian and lemma-naive-completion; algebraization.tex Tag 0A0E, lemma-derived-completion-koszul

proof.text: The hypothesis of [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits] is invertibility of the unit $\eta_K:C\to F(C)$ of [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion] ($r=1$, $a_1=t$), built on the explicit product-fibre model; that proposition reads it through [prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction], whose unit $\kappa_K$ uses the functorial $R\lim$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], as in Step 6. Invertibility does not depend on the model. Put $X_m=C\otimes Q_m$ and let $Z_m$ be the mapping cone of $1\otimes\iota_m:C\to X_m$, a strict tower. On a constant tower $\Delta C$ the map $1-s$ on $\prod_mC^i$ is surjective ($x_1=0$, $x_{m+1}=x_m-y_m$) with kernel the constant sequences, so $C\to F(\Delta C)$ and $C\to R\lim\Delta C$ are isomorphisms (the latter because the Roos triangle of $\Delta C$ splits); $\eta_K$ and $\kappa_K$ are these followed by the two models applied to $\Delta C\to X_\bullet$. Both models commute with cones: $F$ is termwise products and a mapping fibre, and $R\lim$ is exact. Hence $\operatorname{cone}(\eta_K)\cong F(Z_\bullet)$ and $\operatorname{cone}(\kappa_K)\cong R\lim Z_\bullet$, and both are derived limits of $(Z_m)$ [def-weil-derived-limit]: the first because termwise products of complexes are derived products [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact, lem-weil-derived-limit-products-core], the second by its Roos triangle. Two derived limits of one system are isomorphic (TR3 and the five lemma), so $\eta_K$ is invertible iff $\kappa_K$ is. Conversely, if $\kappa_K$ is invertible then so is $\operatorname{comp}_K=c_K\circ\kappa_K$ [prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction]; its components into $\prod_nK_n$ are the $c_n$, so transporting the Roos triangle of $R\lim K_\bullet$ along it gives the triangle of [def-weil-derived-complete]. So the two conventions agree on $X$ and on $Y$.

proof.text:
Apply [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits] to $I=(t)$, using the adic hypotheses verified in Step 4 and intrinsic completeness verified in Steps 6 and 7; its coefficient sheaves $(P_n)_T$, sheafified from $\operatorname{Cont}(\pi_0,P_n)$, are the constant sheaves $(A_n)_T$ by the equivalent description in [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image]. Its required coefficient identification $f^{-1}R_Y\cong R_X$ is [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image], applied to the finite ring tower $A_n$; its projection formulas show that this is the structural map in the item. The proposition states preservation of intrinsic completeness, the finite projection formulas commuting with quotient maps, and the canonical completion composite. Step 7, applied on $Y$, converts that completeness to the convention of the item. Combining the proposition's completion composite with the strict coefficient comparison of Step 5 gives
$$F_RK\xrightarrow{\sim}R\varprojlim_n V_{Y,n}F_nK_n.$$
The projection compatibility of [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison] says that its $n$th projection is $F_R$ of the quotient unit $K\to V_{X,n}K_n$, followed by the normalized coefficient comparison. Thus this is the specified canonical isomorphism, including its strict-tower interpretation.

Finally, [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] identifies derived-complete modules over the completed coefficient sheaf with derived-complete modules over the constant coefficient sheaf, identifies all finite reductions and their transition maps, and identifies the corresponding derived limits. Using the completeness of $F_RK$ from Step 8, applying its natural restriction comparison to the first isomorphism of Step 2 yields $U_YF_RK\cong F_AU_XK$ inside those equivalences. Hence the completed direct image and the constant-$A$ direct image are the same transported functor, with the displayed tower comparison and its normalization.

title: Completed-coefficient pushforward restriction and strict reduction towers
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $t$, and put $A_n=A/(t^n)$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be any morphism of schemes, using the small pro-etale sites with their small-skeleton convention [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For $W=X,Y$ set $R_W=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_W$, the completed coefficient sheaf [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], and let $\underline A_W$ denote the constant sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Use the structural maps $f^{-1}R_Y\to R_X$ induced by the finite projections, and the canonical identifications $f^{-1}\underline A_Y=\underline A_X$ and $f^{-1}(A_n)_Y=(A_n)_X$ [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. Let $D(B)$ be the ordinary unbounded derived category of sheaves of modules over the ring sheaf $B$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $U_W:D(R_W)\to D(\underline A_W)$ and $V_{W,n}:D((A_n)_W)\to D(R_W)$ for termwise restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Denote the K-injective total derived direct images for these ringed topoi by $F_R=Rf_{*,R}$, $F_A=Rf_{*,\underline A}$ and $F_n=Rf_{*,A_n}$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition].

There are canonical natural isomorphisms
$$U_YF_R\xrightarrow{\sim}F_AU_X,\qquad F_RV_{X,n}\xrightarrow{\sim}V_{Y,n}F_n.$$
Their normalization compares the two factorizations of the same composite morphism of ringed topoi, using the K-injective derived-composition comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. For $m\geq n$, the latter comparisons commute with coefficient restriction along $A_m\to A_n$, with the coherence for successive restrictions and quotient maps. For a strict complex of coefficient systems $(M_n)_n$, with $M_n$ an $(A_n)_X$-module complex and transition maps linear through $A_{n+1}\to A_n$, this compatibility is a comparison of derived strict-diagram functors after restriction to $R_X$-module towers, not only an equality of evaluated arrows. Here strict towers and their derived inverse limits are interpreted by [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison].

If $K\in D(R_X)$ is derived $t$-complete [def-weil-derived-complete], form its strict reduction system $K_n=K\otimes^L_{R_X}(A_n)_X$ on one flat-term K-flat representative, with the quotient transitions [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower]. Then $F_RK$ is derived $t$-complete and the preceding comparisons give a canonical natural isomorphism
$$F_RK\xrightarrow{\sim}R\varprojlim_n V_{Y,n}F_nK_n.$$
The right side is obtained by applying total derived direct image to the strict restricted reduction tower and then total derived inverse limit. Under this comparison its $n$-th projection is $F_R$ of $K\to V_{X,n}K_n$, followed by the displayed coefficient-restriction comparison. Finally $U_YF_RK\cong F_AU_XK$ identifies the direct image on complete $R$-modules with the direct image on complete constant-$A$ modules under the equivalences of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence].
